cases.description: Two aliases of one table have independent row bindings and preserve left encounter order.

queries.sql: SELECT child.id AS child_id, ancestor.weight AS parent_weight FROM nodes AS child JOIN nodes AS ancestor ON child.parent = ancestor.id
SELECT child.id AS child_id, ancestor.weight AS parent_weight FROM nodes AS child JOIN nodes AS ancestor ON child.parent = ancestor.id

cases.description: GROUP BY without aggregates supports key expressions and HAVING while retaining first-encounter group order.

queries.sql: SELECT parent + 10 AS bucket FROM nodes GROUP BY parent HAVING parent <> 0
SELECT parent + 10 AS bucket FROM nodes GROUP BY parent HAVING parent <> 0

cases.description: An empty right scan yields an empty inner join but one zero global count row.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows, COUNT(nodes.id) AS ids FROM nodes JOIN other ON nodes.id = other.key
SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows, COUNT(nodes.id) AS ids FROM nodes JOIN other ON nodes.id = other.key

cases.description: A table alias hides its original qualifier even on an empty table.

queries.sql: SELECT nodes.id AS id FROM nodes AS n

cases.description: Duplicate table aliases are rejected even when qualified references otherwise resolve.

queries.sql: SELECT x.id AS id FROM nodes AS x JOIN nodes AS x ON TRUE

cases.description: A nonempty right side contributes no rows to an empty-left outer join; global aggregation still emits its empty group.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(r.id) AS total, COALESCE(MIN(l.id), -9) AS fallback FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(r.id) AS total, COALESCE(MIN(l.id), -9) AS fallback FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id

cases.description: Two empty join inputs produce no grouped rows, even though global aggregation would produce one.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON TRUE GROUP BY l.id
SELECT l.id AS id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON TRUE GROUP BY l.id

cases.description: TRUE OR UNKNOWN is a match, not an unmatched-row condition.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS left_id, r.id AS right_id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON r.flag OR TRUE
SELECT l.id AS left_id, r.id AS right_id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON r.flag OR TRUE

cases.description: FALSE AND UNKNOWN never matches; padding occurs exactly once per left row.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS left_id, r.id AS right_id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON r.flag AND FALSE
SELECT l.id AS left_id, r.id AS right_id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON r.flag AND FALSE

cases.description: An explicit OR/IS NULL predicate intentionally matches NULL keys and preserves duplicate matches.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS id, r.label AS label FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id OR (l.id IS NULL AND r.id IS NULL)
SELECT l.id AS id, r.label AS label FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id OR (l.id IS NULL AND r.id IS NULL)

cases.description: Nullable roots and missing references in an aliased self outer join are both padded.

queries.sql: SELECT worker.id AS id, COALESCE(boss.name, 'root') AS manager FROM staff AS worker LEFT JOIN staff AS boss ON worker.manager = boss.id
SELECT worker.id AS id, COALESCE(boss.name, 'root') AS manager FROM staff AS worker LEFT JOIN staff AS boss ON worker.manager = boss.id

cases.description: A later join may match both stored and introduced NULL through COALESCE.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS id, s.label AS label FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id LEFT JOIN s ON COALESCE(r.next_id, 0) = s.id
SELECT l.id AS id, s.label AS label FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id LEFT JOIN s ON COALESCE(r.next_id, 0) = s.id

cases.description: A WHERE disjunction keeps padded rows and selected matches, without turning rejected matches into padding.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS id, r.v AS v FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id WHERE r.v > 5 OR r.id IS NULL
SELECT l.id AS id, r.v AS v FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id WHERE r.v > 5 OR r.id IS NULL

cases.description: DISTINCT uses the entire projected row before stable sorting and pagination.

queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT r.v AS v, l.id AS id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id ORDER BY v ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3 OFFSET 1
SELECT DISTINCT r.v AS v, l.id AS id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = r.id ORDER BY v ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3 OFFSET 1

cases.description: COUNT of a comparison counts FALSE as a non-null value, not just TRUE.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(v > 0) AS comparable, COUNT(flag) AS known, COUNT(*) AS rows FROM t
SELECT COUNT(v > 0) AS comparable, COUNT(flag) AS known, COUNT(*) AS rows FROM t

cases.description: Aggregate arguments are evaluated per row, including COALESCE and an all-NULL expression.

queries.sql: SELECT COUNT(COALESCE(v, 0)) AS filled, COUNT(NULL) AS absent, COUNT(COALESCE(NULL, flag)) AS flags FROM t
SELECT COUNT(COALESCE(v, 0)) AS filled, COUNT(NULL) AS absent, COUNT(COALESCE(NULL, flag)) AS flags FROM t

cases.description: Defaulting each missing value and defaulting the aggregate result have different totals.

queries.sql: SELECT g AS g, SUM(COALESCE(v, 7)) AS inside, COALESCE(SUM(v), 7) AS outside, COUNT(v + 1) AS incremented FROM t GROUP BY g
SELECT g AS g, SUM(COALESCE(v, 7)) AS inside, COALESCE(SUM(v), 7) AS outside, COUNT(v + 1) AS incremented FROM t GROUP BY g

queries.sql: SELECT label AS label, COUNT(*) AS n FROM t GROUP BY label HAVING label IS NULL
SELECT label AS label, COUNT(*) AS n FROM t GROUP BY label HAVING label IS NULL

cases.description: Different groups with equal projected aggregates collapse, including NULL aggregate results.

queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT SUM(v) AS total FROM t GROUP BY g ORDER BY total DESC NULLS LAST
SELECT DISTINCT SUM(v) AS total FROM t GROUP BY g ORDER BY total DESC NULLS LAST

cases.description: A binding error after a successful nullable query returns only the request error.

queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(v, 0) AS value FROM t
SELECT COALESCE(missing, 0) AS value FROM t

cases.description: ORDER BY binds the projected alias, even when its name matches another source column.

queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(v, -9) AS id, t.id AS original_id FROM t ORDER BY id

cases.description: A known non-null COALESCE prefix does not suppress name binding of later arguments.

queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(1, missing) AS value FROM t

cases.description: An earlier ON clause cannot reference a table introduced by a later join.

queries.sql: SELECT l.id AS id FROM l LEFT JOIN r ON l.id = s.id LEFT JOIN s ON r.next_id = s.id

cases.description: Nesting an aggregate behind COALESCE is still forbidden.

queries.sql: SELECT SUM(COALESCE(SUM(v), 0)) AS total FROM t

cases.description: Every reference outside an aggregate must be grouped, even in a fallback branch.

queries.sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(v), v) AS total FROM t GROUP BY g

cases.description: Boolean ordering preserves equal false rows while explicit NULL placement is independent of direction.

queries.sql: SELECT id AS id, flag AS flag FROM t ORDER BY flag DESC NULLS LAST
SELECT id AS id, flag AS flag FROM t ORDER BY flag DESC NULLS LAST

SELECT id AS id, COALESCE(v, 9) AS value, COALESCE(flag, TRUE) AS enabled, COALESCE(label, 'fallback') AS text FROM t
